criticalError.why: Ceftriaxone is a 3rd-generation cephalosporin â€” a broad-spectrum antibiotic that kills normal gut flora. Cephalosporins are a KNOWN CAUSE of C. difficile, not a treatment. Ordering ceftriaxone for confirmed C. diff makes the infection WORSE by removing bacterial competition while C. diff spores germinate and proliferate.
criticalError.whatShouldHaveBeen: Oral vancomycin 125 mg PO QID x 10 days OR Oral fidaxomicin 200 mg PO BID x 10 days
criticalError.whyOral: The vancomycin molecule is too large (~1,449 Da) to cross the intestinal epithelium. It stays in the gut lumen where C. diff lives. IV vancomycin cannot penetrate the colon and is useless for C. diff. Oral vancomycin also does NOT cause Red Man Syndrome because it is not absorbed systemically.

missed.why: First-line treatment for non-severe C. diff colitis per IDSA 2021 guidelines. Metronidazole is third-line only when vancomycin/fidaxomicin unavailable.
Standard screening â€” expected in every CCS workup.

correctlyAvoided.why: Antimotility agents are contraindicated in C. diff colitis â€” they trap toxins in the colon.

cdiffFirstPrinciples.trigger: Broad-spectrum antibiotics (cephalosporins, clindamycin, fluoroquinolones) kill normal gut flora â†’ C. diff spores survive and germinate
cdiffFirstPrinciples.toxins: Toxin A (enterotoxin) causes fluid secretion and mucosal damage. Toxin B (cytotoxin) is 10x more potent â€” disrupts actin cytoskeleton via Rho GTPase glucosylation.
cdiffFirstPrinciples.pseudomembrane: Yellow-white plaques of fibrin, neutrophils, and necrotic debris on colonic mucosa â€” pathognomonic on colonoscopy.
cdiffFirstPrinciples.severity: Non-severe: WBC <15K + Cr <1.5. Severe: WBC â‰¥15K or Cr â‰¥1.5. Fulminant: hypotension, shock, ileus, megacolon.
cdiffFirstPrinciples.oralVancomycinPharmacology: Molecule size ~1,449 Da â€” too large for paracellular transport across tight junctions. No systemic absorption. Stays in gut lumen. This is WHY oral = effective for C. diff and IV = useless.
cdiffFirstPrinciples.redManSyndrome: IV vancomycin causes histamine release from mast cells â†’ flushing, erythema, pruritus, hypotension. NOT an allergic reaction â€” it's a rate-dependent infusion reaction. Slow the infusion. Oral vancomycin does NOT cause Red Man Syndrome because the drug never enters the bloodstream.
